subject: Nest transect data to deer transect data?

messages.author: 579f340948c2825d
messages.subject: Nest transect data to deer transect data?
parts:
Hey Distance community. I hope all is well.
I have been working with the R package to get estimates for deer populations using pellet surveys. 
Attached is the data file and code which is tailored from the nest transect example.
 
My question is whether the nest example translates to the deer example and if my estimates are accurate. Two sites came out with the same estimates.
In previous studies defecation rates are used. How would that be incorporated into the code or would that be unnecessary. 

Your help and guidance is much appreciated 

Thank you 
-Nick

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Nest transect data to deer transect data?
parts:
Nick

You're off to a good start.  A few points
  • The reason you have the same estimate for two strata is because there are the same number of detections in both strata (14) and you are fitting a common detection function (same function for both strata).
  • I'm guessing this is just a portion of your data to get started.  Otherwise, it is an awkward study design with only a single transect in each stratum.  With that design, you have no measure of encounter rate variability in each stratum.  You're also low on the number of detections for making inference.,
  • The shape of your histograms look fairly good--a bit of heaping at small distances perhaps but both the half normal and hazard rate appear to fit adequately.
  • Are the perpendicular distances measured in meters or feet?  Either way, I'm a little surprised that you are able to detect pellet groups out to 12 (meters or feet).
  • Regarding the inclusion of defecation rates to convert pellet density to deer density; that is something that is not possible to do in the Distance R package just now.  It is an area of programming activity just now and we hope to have multipliers implemented by late this summer.  It is not very hard to do manually; the tricky bit comes it propagating the variability in defecation rates along with the uncertainty in pellet density properly.
    • You can read about including defecation rates (and uncertainty) to convert pellet density to animal density in our online workshop materials:  https://workshops.distancesampling.org/online-course/syllabus/Chapter6/

messages.author: 3908a2da5354fc44
messages.subject: RE: [distance-sampling] Nest transect data to deer transect data?
parts:
Nick,

 

I didn’t look over your code, but if you did the distance sampling correctly you will obtain an estimate of the number of pellets on the landscape. If you can make some assumptions about how long they last on the landscape and defecation rate of the deer, you can simply adjust the pellet estimate accordingly.

 

For example, if you estimates 250 pellets/ha and deer defecate at 1.5 times per day over the 30 days they could exist on the landscape then 250/(1.5*30) is the deer density. If you have estimates of the defecation rate then you could incorporate that error into your density estimate using the delta method. I think this is what Marques et al. did in their paper https://besjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1046/j.1365-2664.2001.00584.x

 

You should be able to  incorporate those defecation rates (with SE) into Distance as an adjustment factor and it will do the hard work for you.

 

Regards,

 

Duane
